subject: Deployment decision worksheet — Hosted evaluation clarifiers and rate/profile questions
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lopez <sarah@acmecommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment decision worksheet — follow-up + quick clarifiers

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the demo with us today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to send a short worksheet to help accelerate the hosted evaluation and clarify the deployment preference (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private). I attached a simple worksheet and included a few quick questions below — short answers are totally fine. Our goal: confirm whether Hosted API will meet your reliability/perf needs in the pilot or if we should propose Dedicated from day one.

Quick clarifiers for the pilot (short bullets):
- Production vs pilot scope: Are you planning to route real customer traffic during the pilot or synthetic/test traffic?
- Peak concurrency: what’s your expected concurrent user sessions at 95th pct during peak hour?
- Average prompt length and average generation token length (tokens or words)
- PII sensitivity: will the prompts contain customer PII or other regulated data?
- Success metric for pilot: latency SLO (p95), cost target ($/1000 tokens), and error budget

Operational questions (hosted specifics):
- Do you need a reserved endpoint with per-route rate caps or can you accept shared pool limits?
- Any requirements for per-request KV-cache warmup or consistent session pinning?

We briefly discussed rate-limits — for context, our Hosted API default for new pilot accounts is 60 rps sustained across the account with 8 concurrent streams to a single chat endpoint; we can raise that for pilots for short windows. If you expect steady high-concurrency or multi-region isolation, Dedicated is usually the more predictable fit.

Next steps I propose: you fill in the attached worksheet with the bullets above, and we’ll map the answers to a recommended pilot configuration (endpoints, token caps, concurrency, and a short runbook). Ben (CC’d) can propose an early hosted quota bump if your concurrency spike is clearly limited in time.

If it’s easier, feel free to reply with short answers here and I’ll populate the worksheet.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Deployment decision worksheet — follow-up + quick clarifiers

Thanks Priya — quick answers inline below. Filling the worksheet this morning and attaching a small traffic sample.

- Production vs pilot: pilot will process live customer chat but only for 5% of sessions (can be routed gradually).
- Peak concurrency: around 120 concurrent chat sessions at 95th pct during US evening peak.
- Avg prompt length: ~45 tokens; avg generation: ~110 tokens.
- PII: minimal — name + order id in a small subset (~8% of prompts). Need to confirm data retention policy.
- Pilot success metrics: p95 latency < 800ms, error rate < 1.5%, cost target approx ~$6 / 1k tokens.

Hosted details: we prefer a managed Hosted endpoint if possible; want per-route rate caps so we can protect the rest of our infra during spikes. Session pinning for KV cache would help, but not required for MVP.

Attaching acme-traffic-sample.csv. Happy to hop on a quick ops call if needed.

—Sarah

Acme Commerce

Subject: Re: Deployment decision worksheet — follow-up + quick clarifiers

Thanks Sarah — this is great and very actionable. A few follow-ups and a recommended quickstart based on your answers: 

Summary of what you provided:
- Live pilot with 5% traffic (~120 concurrent at 95th pct)
- Avg tokens: prompt 45 / response 110 (~155 tokens roundtrip)
- PII in ~8% of messages
- Target: p95 < 800ms, error <1.5%, cost ~ $6 / 1k tokens

Recommended Hosted quickstart (what we can stand up in 48-72h):
- Provision a dedicated Hosted route (logical isolation under your account) with raised quota: 200 rps burst, sustained 75 rps, concurrency 12 streams per route. This should handle the 120 concurrent sessions with headroom for batching.
- Endpoint config: use chat endpoint for session state + KV-caching. Enable session pinning for hot user sessions (best-effort, TTL 30m).
- Data handling: Hosted will not persist input prompts beyond the retention window; we will enable customer-controlled retention and will provide an export for audit. For PII-heavy flows we can enable redaction hooks or propose Private if you need on-prem KMS.
- Rate caps: we will apply a per-route token cap and a hard rps ceiling; Ben can request the pilot quota increase in our internal console immediately after you confirm.

Ben — can you comment on the realistic p95 latency expectation for that config (model xlarge-2 quantized) and whether our default batching settings should be adjusted for Acme's token distribution? Also, please add any DocuSign/PO notes if we need a short-term MSA/credit hold for billing.

Suggested next steps:
1) Sarah confirms you want the raised hosted route for the pilot.
2) Ben opens the pilot quota ticket and we provide the exact token caps + estimated monthly cost for 5% routing.
3) Quick ops sync (30m) to validate network egress, CORS, and webhook retries.

If any of those quickstart bullets push you toward Dedicated/Private, say so — we’ll prepare a Dedicated cost/latency sketch, but given your numbers Hosted looks viable for the pilot.

Thanks — Priya

Hi Priya + Sarah — quick ops note from my side after looking at the sample.

- Latency: with the xlarge-2 quantized model and the token profile you shared (avg 155 tokens), p95 of ~650–750ms is realistic with our recommended hosted route (sustained 75 rps, concurrency 12). We may see occasional cold-starts ~1.2s for very long chains, but KV session pinning should keep warm sessions under your 800ms SLO.
- Batching: I recommend keeping batch window at 20ms and target batch size 8 for the pilot; this balances cost and latency for your distribution.
- Rate caps: I'll request: 200 rps burst / 75 rps sustained on the hosted route and a 1M token/day cap to start; we can tune after the first week.
- Billing/PO: For pilot trials we typically do a short credit hold rather than a full PO; if Acme requires a PO we can fast-track a small pilot SOW.

Action items:
- Priya: confirm we should open the quota ticket and deploy the hosted route.
- Sarah: confirm whether Acme is ok with a hosted pilot with customer-controlled retention and the token/day cap; if you need stricter retention/KMS, we should evaluate Private.

Happy to join the ops sync — ping me with times.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
